Retrieve a specific seller profile snapshot by its unique identifier.

This operation provides access to historical seller profile snapshots that are automatically created whenever a seller updates their shop profile. Each snapshot captures the complete state of the seller's profile at the time of modification, including shop name, description, and logo information.

The snapshot system ensures data integrity and provides an audit trail for seller profile changes. Sellers can use this endpoint to review their profile history and understand how their shop information has evolved over time. The snapshots are immutable and preserved indefinitely for reference purposes.

This operation requires authentication and authorization to ensure that sellers can only access their own profile snapshots. The response includes all the snapshot details captured at the time of creation, allowing sellers to see exactly what their profile looked like at any point in their shop's history.

The snapshot is retrieved from the ecommerce_seller_profile_snapshots table which maintains historical records of all seller profile modifications. This operation returns the complete snapshot data including shop name, description, logo URL, and creation timestamp, providing sellers with visibility into their profile evolution.

Note that this operation only returns snapshots belonging to the authenticated seller, and access to other sellers' snapshots is restricted through ownership validation.
operations.specification: Query the ecommerce_seller_profile_snapshots table by the provided snapshot ID. Validate that the authenticated seller owns the snapshot by checking the ecommerce_seller_id field against the current user's seller ID. Return the complete snapshot data including shop name, description, logo URL, and creation timestamp. Ensure proper authorization checks to prevent unauthorized access to other sellers' snapshots.

parameters.name: snapshotId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the seller profile snapshot to retrieve

responseBody.description: Complete seller profile snapshot data including shop name, description, logo URL, and creation timestamp. Contains all fields captured at the time of the seller profile modification.

Return categories in a hierarchical structure by including parent category relationships. Use Prisma's full-text search capabilities for description field with gin_trgm_ops index. Implement cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Include both active and soft-deleted categories in results to support administrative use cases. Ensure proper authorization - this endpoint should be accessible to all users but may return different data based on authentication status.

Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of product categories with hierarchical organization.

This operation provides comprehensive category browsing capabilities for customers exploring the product catalog and administrators managing category structures. Supports filtering by category name, description content, and parent-child relationships to help users find relevant product categories efficiently.

The response includes category summaries organized hierarchically, allowing customers to understand the category tree structure with one level of nesting. Pagination controls enable browsing large category catalogs while maintaining performance.

Access control ensures that only authorized administrators can view soft-deleted categories while customers see only active categories. The system maintains data integrity by preserving category relationships during filtering operations.

3. Include parent category relationship for hierarchical display
4. Return complete category information including name, description, parent_id, created_at, updated_at

Retrieve detailed information for a specific product category.

This operation provides complete category details including the category name, description, parent category relationship (if applicable), and creation/modification timestamps. Customers can use this endpoint to browse category information while administrators can access it for management purposes.

The category system supports hierarchical organization with one level of nesting. Top-level categories have no parent category reference, while subcategories reference their parent category. This structure enables intuitive product organization and navigation throughout the e-commerce platform.

Related operations include GET /categories for browsing all categories and GET /categories/{categoryId}/products for viewing products within a specific category. Administrative operations for category management are available through separate endpoints requiring appropriate permissions.

Create a new category in the e-commerce platform's hierarchical category system.

This operation allows administrators to create new product categories with optional parent-child relationships supporting one level of nesting. Categories serve as the primary organizational structure for products, enabling efficient customer browsing and product discovery.

When creating a category, the system validates that the category name is unique across all categories and ensures proper hierarchical relationships. Categories can be created as top-level categories (no parent) or as subcategories of existing categories. The operation preserves category integrity by preventing circular references and maintaining the one-level nesting constraint.

Administrators can create categories with descriptive names and detailed descriptions to help customers understand the category scope and purpose. Created categories become immediately available for product assignment and customer browsing.

The operation includes comprehensive validation to ensure data integrity, including unique name enforcement, parent category existence validation, and hierarchical depth constraints. Successful creation returns the complete category object with system-generated identifiers and timestamps.

Related operations include GET /categories for browsing categories, PUT /categories/{categoryId} for category updates, and DELETE /categories/{categoryId} for category removal with product reassignment.

Check that category name is unique across all categories using @@unique([name]) constraint. If parentCategoryId is provided, verify the parent category exists and is not itself a subcategory (maintain one-level nesting). Create new category record with provided data, setting created_at and updated_at timestamps. Return complete category object including system-generated id and timestamps. Ensure proper authorization for administrator access only.

All changes are validated to ensure data integrity, including uniqueness constraints for category names within the same hierarchy level. Category updates preserve historical information through snapshot mechanisms, ensuring that previous versions of category data are retained for audit and reference purposes. The operation automatically updates the modification timestamp to track when changes were made. Circular reference prevention ensures that category hierarchies maintain valid tree structures without infinite loops.

Administrators must have appropriate permissions to perform category updates. The system validates that parent category relationships do not create circular references by traversing the hierarchy and that the updated category structure maintains the platform's one-level nesting constraint. Category names must remain unique within their respective parent contexts to avoid ambiguity in product organization.

Category updates are atomic operations that either succeed completely or fail with appropriate error messages. Failed updates leave the category data unchanged and preserve the existing category state for subsequent modification attempts.

Administrative endpoint for soft deleting a category from the e-commerce platform.

This operation performs a logical deletion by setting the deleted_at timestamp, which preserves the category information for historical audit trails while removing it from active use. Only administrators with appropriate privileges can execute this operation.

When a category is deleted, all products currently assigned to that category are automatically reassigned to have null category_id (uncategorized status) to maintain data integrity. This preserves the relationships in product snapshots while allowing products to be recategorized by administrators as needed.

The category hierarchy structure is maintained through the parent_category_id relationships, and deletion requires validation that no active subcategories exist to prevent orphaned hierarchies. The operation creates appropriate audit trail records for administrative oversight.

Related operations include GET /categories for browsing categories, POST /admin/categories for category creation, and PUT /admin/categories/{categoryId} for category updates. Administrator privileges are required for all category management operations.

Customers can search by product name using text matching, filter by specific categories, specify price ranges, and filter by stock availability. The search supports advanced text matching with partial word matching and relevance ranking.

Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and multiple sorting options including relevance, newest first, price low-to-high, and price high-to-low. Each product result includes essential information for browsing including product name, base price, seller information, and availability status based on variant inventory levels.

The search leverages PostgreSQL's full-text search capabilities with trigram indexing for efficient partial matching. Category filtering ensures products are properly organized according to the platform's hierarchical category system. Price range filtering helps customers find products within their budget constraints.

Security considerations include proper access controls to ensure all users can browse products while maintaining data integrity. The operation returns summarized product information optimized for list displays and search results pages.

The response includes the product's base information (name, description, base price), all available variants with their specific options and pricing, seller shop details, and category information.

Products leverage the platform's snapshot system which creates immutable records of all modifications, though this operation returns the current state. Products inherit from the multi-actor ecosystem supporting customers, sellers, administrators, and super administrators. Each variant includes its SKU code, option values, price override (if different from base price), and current stock quantity tracked through inventory history records.

Seller information includes the shop name and description consistent with the seller profile management requirements. This endpoint supports the platform's order management integration by providing necessary product context for the shopping cart and checkout processes.

For sellers in 'pending_approval' status, product creation is blocked until administrator approval. The product is created with basic information including name, description, category assignment, and base price.

After creation, sellers must add variants to make the product purchasable by customers. Each product belongs exclusively to the creating seller based on authenticated session context. The system enforces name uniqueness within each seller's product catalog to avoid confusion.

The product creation process follows the platform's data integrity requirements - while no snapshot is created for initial creation, subsequent edits will trigger snapshot creation for audit trail purposes through the ecommerce_product_snapshots table. Products cannot be transferred between sellers under any circumstances.

Products are initially created in a draft state and become available for customer viewing once variants are added through POST /ecommerce/seller/products/{productId}/variants operation. Sellers can manage their products through the seller dashboard interface, including adding images, creating variants, and managing inventory.

The operation validates all input parameters against business rules including name length constraints, description requirements, and pricing validation. Category changes require valid category assignments and seller permissions. Product updates trigger immutable snapshot creation that preserves complete product state as audit trails for all modifications.

Product modifications are permanent updates to the product record with historical preservation through the snapshot system rather than soft deletion. This approach maintains data integrity while providing comprehensive audit capabilities.

Retrieve all product images for a specific product in their configured display order.

This operation returns the complete gallery of images associated with the specified product, sorted by their designated position sequence. The first image (position 1) typically serves as the main thumbnail image, while subsequent images provide additional product views from different angles or contexts.

Each image record includes the image URL for display purposes and the position information to maintain the intended gallery ordering. This endpoint is essential for product display pages, mobile applications, and any interface that needs to present the complete product image collection.

The operation validates that the specified product exists before attempting to retrieve its images. If no images are associated with the product, an empty array is returned rather than an error, allowing for graceful handling of products that may not yet have images uploaded.

Image changes are automatically tracked through the platform's product snapshot system to maintain data integrity and audit trails for all product modifications including image additions, deletions, and reordering operations.

Validate image URL format and ensure it points to an accessible image file. Check position validity (must be positive integer). If position conflicts with existing images, adjust ordering accordingly. Create the image record with current timestamp. Update product's updated_at timestamp to reflect modification. Include image changes in product snapshots for audit trail.
operations.description:
Upload a product image to an existing product in the seller's catalog.

This API operation allows sellers to add product images to their listings, supporting multiple images per product with configurable ordering. The first image (lowest position number) serves as the primary thumbnail displayed in product listings and search results. Image uploads are included in product snapshots to preserve the complete audit trail required for financial transaction integrity.

Sellers must have ownership of the target product and the product must be in an editable state (not deleted or pending deletion). The product is identified by the `{productId}` path parameter which must be a valid UUID referencing an existing `ecommerce_products` record owned by the authenticated seller. Image URLs must point to valid, accessible image files in supported formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP) and must not exceed 80,000 characters as defined in the `image_url` database column.

Position values determine display order, with lower numbers appearing first in product galleries. The system validates position uniqueness within the product scope using the `@@unique([ecommerce_product_id, position])` database constraint. If a position conflict occurs, the implementation may adjust ordering or return an error based on business logic.

Images are permanently associated with the product through the `ecommerce_product_id` foreign key constraint. Image changes trigger product snapshot creation through the `ecommerce_product_snapshots` system to maintain transaction integrity for historical orders. When products are displayed in order histories, the images active at the time of purchase are preserved through the snapshot system.

**Database Schema Reference:**
- Main table: `ecommerce_product_images` with columns: `id` (UUID), `ecommerce_product_id` (foreign key), `image_url` (string), `position` (integer), `created_at`, `updated_at` (timestamps)
- Parent table: `ecommerce_products` with soft delete support via `deleted_at` column
- Product ownership: `ecommerce_seller_id` foreign key in `ecommerce_products` table

This operation complements the image deletion capability described in analysis files, where sellers can remove images while preserving them in historical snapshots.

After successful deletion, the remaining images are automatically reordered to fill the gap created by the removed image. This ensures that the product gallery maintains a continuous sequence without missing positions. The first image in the sequence (position 1) always serves as the primary thumbnail for the product.

All image deletions are tracked through the product snapshot system, preserving historical image states for audit trail compliance. This ensures that previous product states with different image configurations remain accessible for order verification and dispute resolution purposes.

The operation requires proper authorization checks to ensure sellers can only delete images from their own products. Administrators have separate endpoints for product oversight and image management.

Each inventory record contains the quantity change amount, reason for the change, and timestamp.

The response shows the chronological sequence of inventory transactions in reverse order (newest first). Positive quantity values indicate stock additions (restocking), while negative values represent stock reductions (orders, adjustments, losses). This comprehensive history supports business intelligence, stock reconciliation, and dispute resolution.

Inventory records are automatically created by the system for order-related activities and can be manually created by sellers for restocking and adjustments. The current stock level for the variant is calculated as the sum of all historical inventory record quantities.

Related operations include adding inventory (POST /sellers/variants/{variantId}/inventory/add) and subtracting inventory (POST /sellers/variants/{variantId}/inventory/subtract) for manual stock management.

When a seller approves a refund request, the system automatically processes the payment reversal and restores the inventory quantities for the affected product variant. Rejected refund requests require the seller to provide a detailed reason explaining the decision.

The operation validates that the refund request exists, is currently pending, and belongs to the seller making the response. Sellers can only respond to refund requests for their own products. The response creates an immutable record of the seller's decision for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

Successful responses return the complete refund response record including the decision, response reason, and timestamps. Failed responses provide detailed error messages indicating the specific validation failure (e.g., invalid refund request, unauthorized access, or invalid decision value).

The operation respects the soft delete functionality implemented through the `deleted_at` field in the `ecommerce_refund_requests` table, ensuring that responses cannot be created for soft-deleted refund requests.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific inventory restoration record by its unique identifier, providing detailed access to restoration records created when cancellation or refund requests are approved. Each restoration record captures the quantity of stock returned to inventory, the business reason for restoration, and links to the specific modification request that triggered it.

This operation provides access to the `ecommerce_modification_inventory_restorations` table data, which serves as the central tracking mechanism for inventory restoration throughout the order lifecycle. The restoration process ensures that when orders are modified after payment or delivery, the corresponding inventory quantities are properly restored to available stock. Each restoration record includes the quantity restored, business reason, and references to both the triggering modification request and the underlying inventory record that was restored.

Inventory restoration records are essential for maintaining complete stock integrity and audit trail compliance. They work in conjunction with the inventory tracking system to provide accurate stock level calculations and support dispute resolution processes. The system automatically creates these records when cancellation or refund requests are approved, capturing the exact quantity returned to inventory and linking it to the specific business event that triggered the restoration.

Access to this operation is restricted to authorized seller users who need to review inventory restoration history for audit purposes, dispute resolution, or inventory management analysis. The response includes complete restoration details along with timestamps for creation and updates, as well as relationships to both the triggering request and the restored inventory record.

Related operations include viewing cancellation requests that triggered restorations (GET /cancellation-requests/{requestId}) and refund requests that triggered restorations (GET /refund-requests/{requestId}), as well as accessing the underlying inventory records (GET /inventory-records/{recordId}). For comprehensive audit trail analysis, sellers should also review the related modification requests and their associated status transitions.
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_modification_inventory_restorations table by the provided restorationId parameter.

Return the complete restoration record including id, quantity_restored, restoration_reason, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at fields.

Include relationship data by joining with cancellation_requests and refund_requests tables to show which modification request triggered this restoration.

Also include the inventory_record relationship to show which inventory record was restored.

Handle cases where the restoration record does not exist by returning appropriate 404 error.

Ensure proper authorization checks - only authorized users should be able to access restoration records.

Return soft-deleted records if they exist, as these records are preserved for audit purposes.

The response should provide a complete view of the inventory restoration operation for transparency and audit trail purposes.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the inventory restoration record to retrieve

operations.description:
Create a new cancellation request for an order item with 'paid' status.

This API operation allows customers to request cancellation for individual order items that are in 'paid' status (payment completed but not yet shipped). The request requires a valid cancellation reason between 10-500 characters and must adhere to strict eligibility criteria: the customer must be the original purchaser, the item must be in 'paid' status, and no shipment must exist for that item.

The cancellation request is automatically routed to the appropriate seller based on the product variant ownership. Upon successful creation, the request enters 'pending' status and starts a 7-day response timer for the seller. If the seller does not respond within 7 days, the system automatically approves the request. The operation creates a permanent record of the request state for audit trail and financial integrity purposes.

Customers can track their cancellation requests through the order management system and will receive notifications when sellers respond. This operation supports the platform's per-item cancellation policy that allows granular control over order modifications while preserving the complete purchase context for other items in the same order.

Create the cancellation request record with 'pending' status and link it to the appropriate seller based on the product variant ownership. Generate an immutable snapshot of the request state for audit trail. Start the 7-day response timer for automatic approval. Return the complete cancellation request object with all related entity references.

Assign a review flag to an administrator for moderation review.

This operation assigns a specific review flag reported by a customer to an administrator for review and resolution. When a customer flags a review as inappropriate or violating platform guidelines, this endpoint allows administrators to take ownership of the moderation process by assigning the flag to themselves.

The assignment process updates the review flag record with the administrator's ID and sets the assignment timestamp. This creates a clear audit trail showing which administrator is responsible for handling each reported review. The flag status transitions from 'pending' to 'under_review' upon successful assignment.

Administrators must have appropriate permissions to assign review flags. The system validates that the flag exists and is in a valid state for assignment (typically 'pending' status). Once assigned, the administrator can review the reported content, investigate the issue, and take appropriate resolution actions such as removing the review, issuing warnings, or dismissing the flag if no violation is found.

This operation is part of the platform's content moderation workflow, ensuring that reported reviews receive proper attention while maintaining accountability and transparency throughout the process. The assignment mechanism helps distribute moderation workload among administrators and prevents duplicate handling of the same reported content.

The response provides confirmation of successful assignment along with updated flag information, including the assigned administrator details and current status. operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_review_flags table to find the flag by ID. Validate that the flag exists and has a status of 'pending' (only pending flags can be assigned). Check that the requesting administrator has appropriate permissions. Update the flag record by setting the ecommerce_administrator_id to the current administrator's ID, updating the status to 'under_review', and setting the assigned_at timestamp to the current time. Return the updated flag information with assignment details.

Implementation steps:
1. Authenticate the administrator making the request
2. Validate the flagId parameter exists in the database
3. Check that the flag status is 'pending' (only pending flags can be assigned)
4. Update the flag record with administrator ID, status change, and assignment timestamp
5. Return the updated flag information
6. Handle error cases: flag not found, invalid status, permission errors

Database operations:
- SELECT * FROM ecommerce_review_flags WHERE id = flagId
- UPDATE ecommerce_review_flags SET ecommerce_administrator_id = adminId, status = 'under_review', assigned_at = NOW(), updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = flagId

Validation rules:
- Flag must exist
- Flag status must be 'pending'
- Administrator must have appropriate permissions
- Administrator ID must be valid

operations.description:
Process customer checkout by converting shopping cart items into a completed order with payment processing.

This operation validates the customer's shopping cart contents, requires selection of a shipping address, processes payment through external gateways, and creates a complete order record. The checkout process ensures all cart items are available and in stock before proceeding with order creation. Upon successful payment processing, shopping cart items are converted to permanent order items and the cart is cleared.

The operation performs comprehensive validation including cart item availability, shipping address verification, and payment method validation. Customers must have at least one valid shipping address configured before checkout can proceed. The payment processing integrates with external payment gateways and creates transaction records for audit purposes.

Successful checkout results in the creation of an order with all items from the shopping cart, deduction of inventory quantities, and generation of payment transaction records. The shopping cart is automatically cleared after successful order creation to prevent duplicate purchases.
operations.specification:
Validate customer shopping cart contents and process checkout to create a new order.

First, retrieve the customer's active shopping cart and validate all cart items:
- Ensure cart exists and belongs to the authenticated customer
- Verify all cart items are available (product variants exist and are in stock)
- Check that quantities do not exceed available inventory
- Remove any invalid items and notify customer

Validate shipping address:
- Customer must select a valid shipping address from their address book
- Verify address has all required fields (recipient, phone, street, city, state, postal code, country)
- Use default address if customer doesn't specify one

Process payment through external gateway:
- Integrate with payment gateway using customer's payment method
- Handle authorization, processing, and reconciliation
- Create payment transaction record with status tracking
- Support retry logic for failed payments

Create order and order items:
- Generate new order record linked to customer
- Convert each valid cart item to order item with purchase-time pricing
- Set initial order item status to 'paid'
- Calculate total order amount from all items

Update inventory and clear cart:
- Deduct purchased quantities from product variant inventory
- Mark shopping cart as deleted (soft delete)
- Preserve cart items for audit trail

Handle edge cases:
- Stock changes during checkout process
- Payment gateway failures
- Invalid shipping addresses
- Concurrent checkout attempts

responseBody.description: Complete order information with all items and payment details

The shipment creation process requires providing carrier information with tracking number and selecting which order items to include in the shipment package.

Upon successful creation, the system automatically updates the status of all included order items to 'shipped' to reflect their progression in the order fulfillment workflow. This status change triggers customer notifications and enables delivery tracking through the provided carrier information. The shipment record preserves the complete shipping context including carrier details, tracking number, and item associations for audit and customer service purposes.

When a customer confirms delivery, the system creates an immutable delivery confirmation record, updates the shipment status to 'delivered', and changes the status of all order items within that shipment to 'delivered'. This confirmation triggers order fulfillment completion and makes the purchased products eligible for customer reviews.

Delivery confirmations serve as audit trail evidence for dispute resolution and provide legal verification that customers received their purchased items. The system also automatically confirms deliveries after 14 days if customers don't manually confirm, but manual confirmation allows for immediate status updates.

Customers can only confirm delivery of shipments that contain their order items. The operation validates shipment ownership before processing the confirmation to prevent unauthorized access to other customers' shipment data.

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

IEcommerceCustomer.IJoin.description: Request body for customer registration. Contains email for authentication, plain text password for secure hashing, display name for personalization, and phone number for customer service communications. All fields are required to create a complete customer profile.
IEcommerceCustomer.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping: email, display_name, phone_number. Password: plain text input for backend hashing. Excluded: id (auto-generated), password_hash (derived), timestamps (auto-generated). Security: Plain password provided for secure hashing server-side.

refresh_token.description: Valid refresh token from the current super administrator session used to obtain new authentication tokens.
refresh_token.x-autobe-specification: Validates against ecommerce_super_administrator_sessions.refresh_token field. Must match an active, non-expired session record.

IEcommerceSuperAdministrator.IRefresh.description: Request body for super administrator token refresh operation containing the refresh token needed to renew authentication session.
IEcommerceSuperAdministrator.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh operation validates the provided refresh token against active super administrator sessions in ecommerce_super_administrator_sessions table. If valid and not expired, creates new access and refresh tokens while maintaining the existing session context. Returns IEcommerceSuperAdministrator.IAuthorized response with new tokens.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token used to generate new authentication tokens for seller sessions.
refresh_token.x-autobe-specification: Extract refresh token from request body and validate against active seller sessions. The token is validated against the ecommerce_seller_sessions table to ensure it's active and not expired before generating new authentication tokens.

IEcommerceSeller.IRefresh.description: Request body for refreshing seller authentication tokens using a valid refresh token. Contains the refresh token that will be validated to generate new access and refresh tokens with updated expiration timestamps.
IEcommerceSeller.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Extract refresh token from request body and validate it against active seller sessions in ecommerce_seller_sessions table. If valid, generate new access and refresh tokens with updated expiration times. Invalidate the old refresh token to maintain security through token rotation.

IEcommerceCustomer.description: Complete customer entity representing a registered user account with personal information, authentication credentials, and account timestamps for a consumer on the e-commerce platform. Includes email address for communication, display name for personalization, phone number for verification, and account lifecycle timestamps.
IEcommerceCustomer.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping: id (primary key), email, display_name, phone_number, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Excluded: password_hash for security.

IEcommerceSuperAdministrator.description: Complete super administrator account entity with administrative metadata. Includes account identification, contact information, creation and update timestamps, and deletion status. Super administrators have the highest level of system access with privileges to manage other administrators and perform system-wide configurations.
IEcommerceSuperAdministrator.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_super_administrators table. SELECT id, email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Exclude password_hash for security. Soft deletion is handled through deleted_at field - if not null, account is deleted but still returned for audit purposes.

IEcommerceSeller.IJoin.description: Request body for seller registration. Contains email address for authentication, password for account security, shop profile information, and session context for audit purposes. The account will be created with 'pending_approval' status requiring administrator review.
IEcommerceSeller.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: Maps: email → email (unique validation), password → password_hash (backend hashing), shop_name → shop_name, shop_description → shop_description, logo_image_url → logo_image_url. System-managed: account_status set to 'pending_approval', created_at/updated_at set to current timestamp. Session context: href/referrer used for audit logging.

IEcommercePlatformEvent.description: Represents a polymorphic subtype relationship between a platform event and various actor types. This unified response type handles the different subtype associations (administrator, customer, seller, super administrator) that can be linked to platform events, providing a consistent interface for retrieving event-actor relationships regardless of the specific actor type.
IEcommercePlatformEvent.x-autobe-specification:
Query the appropriate subtype relationship table based on the actorType discriminator:
- For 'administrator': ecommerce_platform_event_of_administrators table
- For 'customer': ecommerce_platform_event_of_customers table  
- For 'seller': ecommerce_platform_event_of_sellers table
- For 'superAdministrator': ecommerce_platform_event_of_super_administrators table

JOIN with the corresponding actor table to get actor details:
- administrator: JOIN ecommerce_administrators ON actor_id
- customer: JOIN ecommerce_customers ON actor_id
- seller: JOIN ecommerce_sellers ON actor_id
- superAdministrator: JOIN ecommerce_super_administrators ON actor_id
